## Description

Industrial processes usually reject large amounts of waste heat. This heat comes from exothermic reactions in reactors or combustion chambers, and from dissipative equipment that partially degrades electricity into heat, such as intercooled compressors or stirrers. When the resulting hot streams cannot be used for internal heat recovery, the excess heat must be removed with an auxiliary fluid, typically air or water. The choice depends on the required temperature, cost and resource availability.

In a water-based cooling system, circulating water collects the waste heat from the process and is then cooled in a **cooling tower**: a heat and mass exchanger in which the hot water is sprayed into a counter-current flow of ambient air. A small fraction of the water evaporates, which cools the remaining water. The cooled water is pumped back to the process, and the cycle repeats. Because of evaporation, the water can be cooled below the dry-bulb temperature of the air, down to a limit set by the **wet-bulb temperature**.

Recirculation pumps and forced-draft fans consume electricity, and the evaporated, drifted and blown-down water must be replaced by **make-up water**.

## Model

### Thermal performance

The tower is characterised by two temperature differences:

- the **range**, the difference between the return (hot) and supply (cold) water temperatures;
- the **approach**, the difference between the supply water temperature and the ambient wet-bulb temperature.

$$
\Delta T_{range} = T_{out} - T_{in}, \qquad \Delta T_{approach} = T_{in} - T_{wb}
$$ {#eq-ct-range-approach}

Evaporative cooling cannot bring the water below the wet-bulb temperature, so the approach must always be positive ($T_{in} > T_{wb}$). Smaller approaches require exponentially larger towers. Typical design values are a range of 5.5–8.3 K and an approach of 3.3–6.7 K, with an inlet water temperature below 33 °C.

### Wet-bulb temperature

The wet-bulb temperature is computed from the dry-bulb temperature $T$ (°C) and the relative humidity $RH$ (%) with the empirical correlation of Stull (2011):

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{wb} ={} & T \arctan\!\left[0.151977\,(RH + 8.313659)^{1/2}\right] + \arctan(T + RH) - \arctan(RH - 1.676331) \\
& + 0.00391838\,RH^{3/2} \arctan(0.023101\,RH) - 4.686035
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ct-stull}

The arctangents are evaluated in radians. The correlation is valid for 5–99 % relative humidity and −20 to 50 °C at sea-level pressure (except at combined low humidity and low temperature), with a mean absolute error below 0.3 °C.

### Water flows and electricity

The circulating water flow follows from the heat load and the range. The make-up water is estimated with the usual rule of thumb of 0.085 % of the circulating flow per °F of range (the factor 1.8 converts K to °F). The electricity of pumps and fans is proportional to the heat load.

$$
\dot m_{w} = \frac{\dot Q_{max}}{c_{p,w}\,\Delta T_{range}}, \qquad
\dot V_{mu} = 0.00085 \cdot 1.8\,\dot V_{w}\,\Delta T_{range}, \qquad
\dot E_{CT} = e_{CT}\,\dot Q_{max}
$$ {#eq-ct-flows}

### Investment cost

The tower investment cost (EUR, 2008) is given by the correlation below, with $\dot m_w$ in t/h and temperatures in K or °C. It is updated with the CEPCI and annualised over the lifetime $n$ at interest rate $i$:

$$
C_{CT} = \frac{746.49}{0.066}\,\dot m_w^{0.79}\,\Delta T_{range}^{0.57}\,\Delta T_{approach}^{-0.9924}\,(0.022\,T_{wb} + 0.39)^{2.447}
$$ {#eq-ct-cost}

$$
\tau = \frac{i\,(1+i)^n}{(1+i)^n - 1}, \qquad
C_{inv,2} = C_{CT}\,\frac{CEPCI_{2020}}{CEPCI_{2008}}\,\tau
$$ {#eq-ct-annuity}

## Parameters

### Input parameters

| Variable | Description | Type | Default | Bounds | Unit |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|:--|:--|
| `Cool_Tin` | Supply (cold) water temperature | Decision | 13 | 5 – 20 | °C |
| `Cool_Tout` | Return (hot) water temperature | Context | 30 | 25 – 40 | °C |
| `Cool_Qmax` | Reference heat load | Literature | 100 000 | 10 000 – 500 000 | kW |
| `cp_water` | Specific heat capacity of water | Literature | 4.2 | 4.0 – 4.3 | kJ/(kg·K) |
| `Tdrybulb` | Dry-bulb temperature | Context | 20 | −10 – 45 | °C |
| `RelatHum` | Relative humidity | Context | 40 | 10 – 100 | % |
| `Cool_Elec` | Electricity per unit of heat removed | Literature | 0.021 | 0.005 – 0.05 | kW~el~/kW~th~ |
| `dtmin_gas` | $\Delta T_{min}/2$ contribution, gas streams | Context | 8 | 5 – 30 | °C |
| `dtmin_liq` | $\Delta T_{min}/2$ contribution, liquid streams | Context | 5 | 2 – 15 | °C |
| `dtmin_2ph` | $\Delta T_{min}/2$ contribution, two-phase streams | Context | 2 | 1 – 10 | °C |
| `n` | Lifetime | Context | 40 | 10 – 60 | year |
| `i` | Interest rate | Context | 0.06 | 0.01 – 0.15 | – |
| `CEPCI_2020` | Cost index, 2020 | Context | 596.2 | – | – |
| `CEPCI_2008` | Cost index, 2008 (correlation base year) | Context | 575.4 | – | – |

: Input parameters of the cooling tower model {#tbl-ct-inputs .striped}

### Calculated parameters

Values computed with the default inputs.

| Variable | Description | Formula | Value | Unit |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|:--|
| `Twetbulb` | Wet-bulb temperature | @eq-ct-stull | 12.32 | °C |
| `range` | Temperature range | `Cool_Tout - Cool_Tin` | 17 | K |
| `approach` | Approach temperature | `Cool_Tin - Twetbulb` | 0.68 | K |
| `E_ref_CT` | Electricity consumption | `Cool_Elec * Cool_Qmax` | 2 100 | kW |
| `water_flow` | Circulating water flow | `Cool_Qmax / cp_water / range * 3600 / 1000` | 5 042 | t/h |
| `water_vflow` | Circulating water volume flow (1 t/m³) | `water_flow` | 5 042 | m³/h |
| `watermu_CT` | Make-up water | `0.00085 * 1.8 * water_vflow * range` | 131.1 | m³/h |
| `Annuity` | Capital recovery factor | @eq-ct-annuity | 0.0665 | – |
| `CTCost` | Tower investment cost | @eq-ct-cost | 25.5 × 10^6^ | EUR |
| `Cinv2_CT` | Annualised investment cost | @eq-ct-annuity | 1.75 × 10^6^ | EUR/y |

: Calculated parameters of the cooling tower model {#tbl-ct-outputs .striped}

## Units and streams

The model has a single unit, `CoolingTower`, of type **utility**. Its size multiplier (between 0 and 100 times the reference capacity) and its existence are optimisation variables. The investment cost is fully proportional to the size (`Cinv2 = Cinv2_CT`); fixed and variable operating costs are zero.

### Resource streams

| Connector | Layer type | Direction | Flow | Unit | Conditions |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `ELECTRICITY` | Electricity | in | `E_ref_CT` | kW | – |
| `WATER` | Mass (make-up water) | in | `watermu_CT` | m³/h | 25 °C, 1 bar, liquid H~2~O |

: Resource streams of the `CoolingTower` unit {#tbl-ct-resources .striped}

### Heat streams

A single cold stream takes the circulating water from the supply to the return temperature and absorbs the process waste heat. The heat cascade is the default one.

| Stream | T~in~ | T~out~ | H~in~ | H~out~ | $\Delta T_{min}/2$ | $\alpha$ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Cooling tower heat | `Cool_Tin` | `Cool_Tout` | 0 kW | `Cool_Qmax` | `dtmin_liq` | 1 kW/(m²·K) |

: Heat stream of the `CoolingTower` unit {#tbl-ct-heat .striped}
